title: Headings must not be empty
summary: A heading element has no text, so screen readers announce a heading with nothing in it. Add text to it or remove the element.
problem:
A heading such as

has no text content and no accessible name. It is often left behind by a template or a page builder when a field is left blank, or it holds only an image with no alt text.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users who move through a page by headings land on one that says nothing, which is confusing and wastes time. It also adds a meaningless entry to the page outline that search engines read.
steps: Find the empty heading in your template, page builder or CMS. The scan result shows the exact markup.
If the heading should have a title, fill in the text, or make your template print the heading only when there is text to show.
If it exists only for spacing, delete it and use CSS margin or padding instead.
If it contains only an image, add alt text to that image so the heading has a name.

whyItMatters: This is a recommended practice rather than a WCAG failure. An empty heading is noise in the outline that people with screen readers use to find their way, and it is usually a quick template fix.
howToCheck: Open a headings list in your browser accessibility tools or an extension and look for entries with no text. In the page source, search for heading tags with nothing between them.
